session.title: 1.0.37: forget a Codex window whose server refuses the connection (SW207)
session.purpose: Carry out SW207 from the hub port-exhaustion trace: 68 of 69 Windows Codex window session files belonged to windows whose terminals were killed, and Switchy retried all of them every 60 s at once (6,229 refused loopback connects in 96 minutes, one burst coinciding with Tcpip event 4231). Stop retrying windows whose server is gone, release 1.0.37, install it on the workstation and verify live.
outcomes: Windows: a refused connect to a window's server (tungstenite Error::Io, ErrorKind::ConnectionRefused / os error 10061) now deletes that window's .token, .refresh and .session files and logs one line ('...: the connection was refused, so its window has closed; removed its session files'). The wrapper writes .session only after its server answered, so a refusal means the server exited. Every other connect error (10055, timeouts, auth, protocol) keeps the 60 s retry and the files.

WSL: applied the same rule, since the relay distinguishes a gone socket with certainty. 'codex app-server proxy --sock' (codex-cli 0.162.1) prints 'failed to connect to socket at <path>' with 'No such file or directory (os error 2)' when the socket link is missing and 'Connection refused (os error 111)' when a stale socket has no listener. The relay's stderr, previously discarded, is now read for the relay's whole life (first 4 KB kept, the rest drained so the pipe never fills); a failed handshake whose stderr carries that line with os error 2 or 111 forgets the window. Anything else keeps the retry. The WSL socket symlinks themselves are left in the directory (outside the task's file list).

Tests: two new tests in proxy::codex_engine (refused -> .session/.token/.refresh deleted; a 401 from a live listener -> all kept and still listed; the WSL stderr classifier against the observed texts and negatives). cargo test --lib proxy::codex_engine: 10 passed. The GitHub Tests workflow on the public push (run 39273206422, Linux, full vitest and cargo suites) passed.

Released v1.0.37 on registered2nd/switchy (Latest) with exe, msi and the Apple Silicon dmg from build-macos.yml run 39273223759; the dmg was checked (7z integrity OK, CFBundleShortVersionString 1.0.37, Mach-O arm64, contains the new code's strings) and all three asset digests match installers/. The NSIS helper-DLL cache was not mis-hashed this time. Private main pushed; publish_public.sh fast-forwarded the public repo to 2edd8151, the release target.

Installed 1.0.37 on the workstation by the one-command reinstall at 07:51:33 local; port 15721 up in 4 s. Its first sweep removed 68 Windows and 6 WSL closed windows' files; ~/.codex/switchy-sessions/ then held only 3619067d... (ws://127.0.0.1:54806, listener codex pid 78600) and WSL only 91020-17871.sock.session (server running). A probe Codex window opened afterwards (ws://127.0.0.1:64674) was connected and signed in to provider=f7649e3f at 07:52:30; killing its terminal tree left its files and Switchy removed them 3 s after its server went away. 13 minutes after the install: 0 'actively refused' lines, 0 codex_engine warnings.
Not updated, per the task: the laptop and another user's Mac run 1.0.36; another user's PC has 1.0.36 installed and Switchy not running.

Reported to the hub session (projects-b4) rather than fixed: stale WSL socket symlinks remain in ~/.codex/switchy-sessions/ (4 now, pointing into /tmp/codex-daemon-1000/, which also holds many old .lock files); every proxied request logs two 'No pricing for model' warnings for gpt-6.1-sol and claude-opus-5-5; three pre-existing unused-import warnings in the lib test build.
session.latest_summary: 1.0.37 forgets a Codex window, on Windows or WSL, the first time its server refuses the connection, ending the per-minute burst of refused loopback connects. Released for Windows and Apple Silicon; installed and verified live on the workstation only.

current_focus.summary: Switchy 1.0.37 is the latest public Windows and Apple Silicon release; it forgets a Codex window whose server refuses the connection. It runs on the workstation; the laptop and another user's Mac run 1.0.36, and another user's PC has 1.0.36 installed and not running. On the workstation Claude is locked on registered2nd (ccb19499) at the user's request; its weekly reset reads 2026-10-25, which the user had expected before 10/22, and he has not said whether to keep that lock or move it to the Apple-relay account that resets 10/22. The requested work is complete; await the user's feedback. Earlier renewal, restart, WSL, rotation and proxy-off checks stay pending under their triggers.

next_actions.summary: Confirm account-proxy coverage on the next natural Claude sign-in or renewal while Owen is selected, without forcing a new login. Claude Code's own exchange should log '[connect_tunnel] platform.claude.com:443 via socks5://82.26.163.142:45001'. For Switchy's renewal, observe '[claude_pool] refreshing login for provider=98e00f12...' and the successful refreshed-login message; the enforced per-account client route is owned by proxy/http_client.rs. Windows/WSL HTTPS_PROXY and NO_PROXY, UK exit probes and telemetry tunnels were verified; a live sign-in/renewal using this route remains unobserved. Connection failures must stop rather than fall back to direct; country observations only warn.

CONFIRM THE RESTART PATH ON STEPHEN'S NEXT WINDOWS RESTART (1.0.29). In C:/Users/Administrator/.switchy/logs/switchy.prev.log after 'Session ending; handing the live configs back': '[session-end] claude/codex/gemini handed back', '[session-end] ... in WSL handed back', then 'Live configs handed back for the session end'. 'did not finish in 4 seconds' with the last [session-end] line shows which step stalls (Windows step = database lock, WSL step = WSL I/O); fix that step. In switchy.log: Switchy started within seconds of login (window hidden, launched with --autostart from HKCU Run), '[auto_launch] start at login on', proxy on 15721, and Claude Code / Codex answer without ECONNREFUSED.

CONFIRM CLAUDE LOGINS STAY IN STEP WITH WSL (1.0.27). In switchy.log, when an account WSL is signed in to renews: '[claude_pool] provider=... took the newer login from WSL' or 'wrote the refreshed login through to WSL', and no new 'invalid_grant' 'Refresh token not found or invalid' in account_switches/provider_health. WSL's ~/.claude/.credentials.json and ~/.switchy/accounts/<id>/credentials.json for that account should carry the same refreshToken after each renewal.

CONFIRM ROTATION AND CODEX FAILOVER ON LIVE TRAFFIC (1.0.25/1.0.26). In C:/Users/Administrator/.switchy/logs/switchy.log and the switchy.db account_switches table: (a) when an account's five-hour window resets while another serves, a switch back to it with reason 'recovered' and detail "Another account's weekly limit resets sooner"; (b) a Codex turn refused for usage that continues an earlier one logs '[CodexWS] provider=... websocket closed (turn refused for usage; Codex resends it in full)' and the turn then completes on the next account with no error in Codex. GET http://127.0.0.1:15721/switchy/accounts shows current account, pool order, quota and atLimit per account.

VERIFY LOCAL PROXY OFF WITH AN OPEN CODEX WINDOW. the user was asked to turn Local proxy off in Settings > Pool, then use a Codex window opened while the proxy was on. Confirm in C:/Users/Administrator/.switchy/logs/switchy.log that "Proxy turned off; its listener stays up..." was logged, that the Codex window's later [Codex] requests still reached the proxy and answered, that netstat shows 127.0.0.1:15721 still LISTENING, and that Settings shows the proxy as off. Turning it back on must reuse the listener.

QUIT CASE WAITS ON STEPHEN. Quitting Switchy still breaks Codex windows opened under the proxy. He was offered a warning on quit naming the open Codex windows (small) or running the proxy as a process that outlives Switchy's window (large); he has not chosen. Build nothing until he does.
If the user directs request logging to be enabled, first make the Usage page's Turn on button apply to the running proxy, then enable it for Claude, Codex, and Gemini.
